transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, and I'm sorry if it sounds a little silly, but... I guess I've just been having a hard time lately with, well, how I look. 

It's probably not a huge deal, but I just can't stop thinking that the left side of my face is... off. Like, whenever I have to look at an ID photo, or if I have my camera on for my online college classes, my nose and my jaw just look completely crooked. I've brought it up to a few people, and they always say they don't see it, which is nice of them to say, but... I don't know. I just feel like everyone in the CNC lab at work is noticing my face before they even notice the programs I'm running. 

Um, does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you help with.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to fix or hide that part of your face, or comparing it to other people's faces?

Um... yeah. I guess I do a little bit of that. I mean, everyone wants to look presentable before they leave the house, right? But... well, I probably take it a bit too far. 

I hope it doesn't sound too weird, but before I leave for school, I kind of... get stuck. I'll be at the bathroom mirror, and then I'll pull out my phone camera just to double-check how the angles look. And I'll keep trying to fix my hair, or I'll keep changing my shirts to see if a different fit hides my jaw better. I even ask my mom if my face looks weird, which I know is probably really annoying for her. 

It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but... sometimes I get caught up doing all that for so long that I actually end up missing my lab completely. Or if I do make it to class, I'm just so wiped out from stressing about it that I can't even focus on my work. 

Um, is that the kind of thing you meant? I really hope I'm not sounding too crazy...
How long have you been feeling this way about the left side of your face, and has it gotten worse over time?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe a few years? I think it started back in high school, but it wasn't a big deal back then. Just normal teenage stuff, you know? Like, everyone is a little insecure when they're a teenager. 

But... I guess it has gotten a little harder lately. Especially since starting college and working in the lab. I just... I really want to make a good impression on people, and I worry that my face is getting in the way of that. It's not like I'm obsessed or anything, I just... I probably think about it more than I should. 

I'm sorry, I don't know the exact timeline. I hope that's okay? I just know it feels like it's taking up a lot more of my energy these days than it used to. Does that help answer your question?
Has this concern about your face caused you significant distress or affected your ability to function in school, work, or social situations?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I try really hard not to let it get in the way of things, but... like I mentioned before about missing the lab sometimes... it has been happening a bit more often. 

I'm really sorry if this sounds bad, but I've actually missed a few of my shop shifts, too. It's just... sometimes I get so stuck trying to make sure I look okay that I just can't get myself out the door. My faculty mentor actually pulled me aside recently and said my work placement might be in jeopardy if I keep missing hours. I felt terrible about it, I really did. I'm usually a very responsible person, I promise. 

And, um, socially... I guess I've pulled back just a tiny bit. I used to play soccer and do some volunteering, but I kind of stopped going. I just... I don't really want people looking at me when my face is so messed up. It's just easier to stay home, you know? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely non-functional or anything. I'm really trying my best to keep it together. Is it normal to struggle with this kind of stuff?

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms, including persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (face), repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, reassurance seeking), and significant distress/impairment in functioning (missing work/school, social withdrawal), are most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). Other differential diagnoses such as substance-induced disorders (F10.11-F19.11) have been ruled out as there is no evidence of substance use contributing to the symptoms.
